caption:
Google opened up Gemini 4 Carbon, which it calls its strongest model for cybersecurity and long, multi-step work.
Google says security firm Wiz used it to find unknown flaws at two major software providers in under two hours.
AI Ultra subscribers get it in the Gemini app now. The API price doubles after November 30.

site_article.headline: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers and AI Ultra subscribers
site_article.dek: The model, which Google calls its strongest for cybersecurity and long agentic work, launches at an introductory API price that runs through November 30.
site_article.summary: Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon to paying developers, businesses and Google AI Ultra subscribers on November 10, 2026, after two weeks of limited access for cybersecurity defenders. Introductory API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30.
site_article.seo_title: Google Gemini 4 Carbon now available: access, price, uses
site_article.seo_description: Gemini 4 Carbon is out for AI Ultra subscribers and paying developers. Who gets it, what it costs before and after November 30, and what Google claims.
site_article.answer_summary: Gemini 4 Carbon is available from November 10, 2026 to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode and Antigravity, and to paying developers through the Gemini API at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until November 30.
site_article.hero_alt: Portrait photo of Google CEO Sundar Pichai smiling, with the Gemini logo on the side.

paragraphs.text: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon broadly available on November 10, 2026, opening the model to paying developers, businesses, scientists and subscribers to its Google AI Ultra plan. In a post for developers, the company described Carbon as its strongest model, with frontier performance in cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities, built for sustained agentic workflows.

The release ends a period of about two weeks in which Carbon was limited to a small group of cybersecurity defenders through Google DeepMind's Fairwind Program, according to Digital Trends and Runtime Wire. Runtime Wire reported that Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google DeepMind's senior vice president and Google's chief AI architect, announced the wider release.
Where Carbon fits next to Argon

Carbon sits above Gemini 4 Argon in Google's lineup. According to 9to5Google, Google describes Argon as the right choice for most software engineering and knowledge work, while Carbon is meant for tasks that test the limits of a model, such as complex multi-step coding and debugging and open-ended scientific research. Argon remains available to AI Pro subscribers and higher tiers.

Digital Trends reported that Carbon uses more tokens than Argon and spends that extra effort exploring options and checking its own answers. Google's developer post points to multi-step work in software engineering, full-stack web development and scientific research as the main targets, and says the model has stronger alignment and more reliable follow-through.
What Google claims the model can do

In its announcement, as summarized by Digital Trends, Google said Carbon ranked first on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR and Zapier's AutomationBench, and that its cost per task was less than half that of the next best model from another company. Google did not name that rival model or publish absolute cost figures in the announcement Digital Trends described.

Google also cited customer examples. Security firm Wiz used Carbon to scan two major software-as-a-service providers and found previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities in under two hours, work Google said would normally take weeks. Axiom Bio used the model to identify toxicity mechanisms its team had not found before and is moving production scientific analyses to Carbon and Argon, according to the same report.

Developers also get an early look at a feature called /swarm in Google Antigravity, in which Carbon handles design, coordination and review while lighter, faster models work on other tasks in parallel, Digital Trends reported.
Who can use it and what it costs

Google AI Ultra subscribers can use Carbon in the Gemini app, in AI Mode in Search and in Google Antigravity, with the app rollout starting on November 10, according to 9to5Google. Developers can reach it through the paid tier of the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Android Studio, and businesses through Gemini for business. Scientists can apply for six months of free access to Argon and Carbon, and cybersecurity defenders can apply to the Fairwind Program.

Introductory API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, according to 9to5Google and Runtime Wire. 9to5Google reported that the price then rises to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens.

The launch puts the security claims at the center of the pitch. The benchmark rankings and the Wiz and Axiom Bio results come from Google and its partners, not from independent testing, so outside evaluations over the coming weeks will show how much of the advantage holds up. The short introductory window also gives developers a cheap period to compare Carbon with Argon and with rival models before the price doubles.
The next signal to watch is independent benchmark results and developer reports on whether Carbon's higher token use still delivers a lower cost per task once the price rises on December 1.
